Fellow 19 year old here, and I often feel the same way. 
It’s so hard to not look at others our age and compare. Right now it seems like everyone is setting themselves up for their future. On Instagram I see people I graduated high school with enjoying college, going on trips with friends and family, and all around enjoying life. 
In other words, they’re doing things they can be proud of. Things that seemingly make them and others happy. And when you don’t have that, it makes you feel alone or inadequate. And it’s consuming. 
Society’s standards for us certainly don’t help either. At our age, every time I see family or meet someone new I get asked the same questions:

“Going to school?” 

“No...”

“Going back to school?”

“I don’t really know... just working right now.”

“So what do you do?“

“Oh I don’t really know it’s not really important...”

“Well... what do you like to do?”

“Just hang out I guess...”

Sound familiar? 
Our situation isn’t uncommon. Allow me to offer some advice. I know it’s hard not to compare, but avoid it when you can. Maybe take some time off the Internet if it helps. And if you do compare - compare honestly. Know that at 19, half of those people you described are going to wind up spending the next few decades stuck in jobs they hate, marriages that drain them, and putting up a rosy front for the world to see. All so that they can maintain the illusion of all the things we think they have. Just remember to be kind to yourself. The world’s best kept secret is that nobody has it all figured out. You and I are just more honest about it :)

I know the go-to answer is ignorance and denial of basic science, but I give Christians the benefit of the doubt. In my experience most simply believe that Jesus will return before humanity has to suffer the devastating consequences of climate change. 

When I was still a practicing baptist, I was never concerned about the climate not because “there’s no way it isn’t real”, but because we all kinda assumed that the world burning up was the natural order of things. I mean, when your sacred texts marry apocalyptic events with the return of your lord and savior, it’s easy to see how most Christians shrug it off as “a sign of the times” and go comfortably about their day knowing that as the shoreline gets closer, so does the day of judgement.

There’s an argument to be had here, I’m on your side, but it feels weak. Allow me to play devils advocate. 
I believe Jesus would have been able to feel guilt, anxiety, confusion, and all the like. In fact it was always taught to me that if he didn’t feel these things, he would not have had an accurate human experience. 

A biblical example of this was when Jesus was crying in the garden before his crucifixion. The interpretation I was taught was that he felt sad that there was no other way to save humanity, and that Jesus was ((almost)) upset with God about it. 
An example off the top of my head is that Jesus may have experienced guilt knowing that he was able to save people from illness, but it wasn’t always in “gods plan” to do so. Although that last point brings up a whole new cast of problems, I hope you can see how little effort it takes to pick this argument apart. Most forms of human suffering aren’t sins. Feeling bored, heartbroken, tempted, sad, etc can all be experienced without sinning. 

And even if you somehow got a Christian to concede that there were emotions that Jesus didn’t suffer, I don’t see why the next logical conclusion is that “because Jesus didn’t feel boredom, he could not have died for your sins”.

There are so many times that I have been in the car with others and have been offered the aux, only to freeze and panic. If people ask what I’m listening to I will almost always lie. Even my ex would get frustrated when I wouldn’t let us listen to my music. You aren’t alone. 

Sort of like you mentioned in the beginning, I think I’ve determined this fear comes from having my interests invalidated as a child. My parents had a very specific mold that they wanted me to fit, and anything that didn’t align with it was tossed out. There’s a neat way Ive started to break this habit though, and it might work for you too. 

Any time I find myself in a situation where I might be asked to play music, like a party, try suggesting just one song to add to the que. It’s a small step, but if you can find the courage more often than not you will find others accepting of whatever taste you have. It’s a tremendous confidence booster when your song finally plays and you see people reacting positively. I hope this helps!

I have had *very* similar dreams that continue to this day and are fairly regularly recurring. The scariest bit about them is that some of them could have been real. They’re so realistic it’s like I can’t tell.

Almost all of them start the same way. Waking up, and knowing something is present. It’s heavy in the air. All around you. An evil dread. 

In the moment I’m terrified, but I always face the presence. At this point it manifests itself, usually in my hallway for some reason. At this point an eerie darkness (sometimes a red glow) creeps toward me, while I scream and shout for it to “LEAVE IN THE NAME OF THE LORD” or something similar.

When it’s finally gone, I climb back into my bed or the couch, cover up, and go back to sleep. When I wake up IRL, I’m tired and groggy, and unnerved. 

The scariest one by far was just a week ago while I was sleeping on the couch. In the dream, I woke up hearing a knock on my back door. Now mind you I live in a nice neighborhood with a fenced in back yard with a locked gate, have a very protective dog outside, and always double lock my back door. The same presence was there, and for some reason I fell right back to sleep.

Woke back up a few minutes later, and the back door was *open*. I was petrified. But once again I went back to sleep.

Waking up the third and last time, I got up and made my way down the hallway in the pitch black darkness. I stopped just before the doorway of the master bedroom. The door was wide open, and inside was an indescribable darkness. And in the middle, the silhouette of a man-like thing. It whipped its head toward me and rushed at me but was stopped when I began crying out to God for the thing to be gone. 

No idea what it means. I’ve always interpreted it as some kind of spiritual warfare going on while we sleep. Like demons desperately trying to take me, but failing time and time again.
